title.narrative: Electricity Sector Efficiency and Supply Reliability Program

description.narrative: The Program development objectives are to improve efficiency of the electricity sector, maintain the supply of transmission grid-connected renewable energy and the reliability of electricity service, and strengthen NEPCO's governance.

The development objectives of Electricity Sector Efficiency and Supply Reliability Program for Jordan are to improve efficiency of the electricity sector, maintain the supply of transmission grid-connected renewable energy and the reliability of electricity service, and strengthen NEPCO's governance. This paper seeks an Additional Financing (AF) of 250 million US dollars under the Electricity Sector Efficiency and Supply Reliability Program for Results (PforR). The AF would require extending the PforR's closing date by 18 months to February 29, 2028. The PforR supports the implementation of Phase 1 of the Government program (2023–2025). In particular, it focuses on improving the operational efficiency of the electricity sector through implementing the cost saving and revenue enhancement measures, maintaining the supply of transmission grid-connected renewable energy, ensuring the reliability of the electricity service, and strengthening NEPCO's governance. Building on the successful implementation of the PforR, the AF would strengthen the Bank's support to the Government's efforts in scaling up the positive impact of Phase 1 on NEPCO's financial standing. The PforR and the AF continues to serve as a platform for collaboration between the Government and the World Bank (and other development partners). The Bank's support through the AF to scale-up the targets of Phase 1, and extend it to 2027 is important to improve the readiness of the Government to advance the implementation of Phase 2 of its program towards setting NEPCO back to adequate financial footing. The AF will address the Government's need to optimize the financing resources to reduce borrowing costs for Program implementation. The AF is a crucial step to maximize the cost saving and other improvements before the Government fully embarks on Phase 2 to restore NEPCO's long-term financial viability under Phase 2.

title.narrative: New investments in transmission-connected electricity generation and storage are economically justified, financially efficient, and climate responsive

baseline.value: New transmission connected generation investments are not always economically justified, financially efficient, and climate responsive.

target.value: New transmission-connected generation and storage investments are: (a) consistent with NEPCO's Generation Master Plan, exclusive of fully grant-financed projects, which takes into account the target of at least 31% of renewable energy in the electricity supply mix by 2030, including transmission and distribution-connected generation; and (b) competitively procured consistent with the Public Procurement By-Law and PPP Legislation.

comment.narrative: NEPCO and MEMR have started the process to secure (i) 580 MW combined cycle gas generation and (ii) 200 MW solar PV generation. Both projects are part of NEPCO's 2023 Masterplan.

baseline.value: NEPCO has been partially implementing the elements of newly-introduced corporate governance structure

target.value: (a) NEPCO continues to implement the adopted 3-year financing plan for its operations; (b) the Government as shareholder maintains the Board of NEPCO with strengthened composition, role, and responsibilities in accordance with the Charter of NEPCO; (c) the Risk and Audit Committee maintains its composition and role and continues implementing its responsibilities consistent with the Board of NEPCO Resolution No. 87, dated October 4, 2020; (d) the Strategy and Risk Management Function continues to be implemented in accordance with the Board of NEPCO Resolution No. 50, dated August 22, 2021; (e) the Board of NEPCO continues reviewing, approving and monitoring implementation of NEPCO's strategy, budget, and risk profile with defined financial and non-financial KPIs, and (f) align its accounting policies with IFRS in line with the conclusions of the gap analysis study that will completed in 2025.

comment.narrative: The recent Cabinet reshuffle resulted in a few vacant positions in NEPCO's board of directors.
